title: Microsoft Teams: Copilot in the Queues app on mobile
summary: The briefing's rollout, licensing and recording requirements are supported by Microsoft's notice and documentation. The controls are documented, including the recording PowerShell restriction explained below the table; the licence-assignment API note should name its request-body properties.

claims.where: licensing.notes; Cost and licensing; Open questions
claims.claim: No separate feature price, meter or Copilot Credits charge is published in the cited material.
claims.quote: Searched: Queues app Copilot credits pricing; Microsoft Teams Queues app Copilot licensing billing meter. Read MC1552391, manage-queues-app, copilot-license-options, Teams add-on licensing, voice applications licensing; billing search results name other services.

claims.claim: The Queues app can take up to 48 hours to appear after Teams Premium licensing.
claims.quote: Once a user is licensed for Teams Premium, it can take up to 48 hours for Queues app to be available in the Teams client.

claims.claim: Queues app is enabled by default for voice-enabled Teams users with Teams Premium and Teams Phone.
claims.quote: Queues app is enabled by default for all Teams users in your organization who are assigned both a Teams Premium and Teams Phone license and who are voice enabled.

claims.claim: The Queues app supports iOS and Android mobile clients.
claims.quote: The Queues app is currently supported on Teams desktop, Mac, and Virtualized Desktop Infrastructure (VDI) clients, Teams phones (touch devices only), and iOS and Android mobile clients.

claims.claim: The October 27, 2026 Copilot release notes describe Copilot Chat after a call in the Queues app.
claims.quote:
October 27, 2026
Updates released between October 13, 2026, and October 27, 2026.
Use Copilot Chat after a call in Queues app [Windows, Mac]

claims.claim: The documented Queues app flow opens a recorded call in unified call history and launches the Copilot Chat sidecar from Recap.
claims.quote: Navigate to the unified call history in the Queues app, select the recorded call record, and launch the Copilot Chat sidecar from within the Recap tab.

claims.claim: Microsoft Learn has no dedicated page for this mobile Copilot feature at the time of writing.
claims.quote: Searched: Copilot Queues Mobile; Microsoft Teams Copilot Queues app mobile shared call history admin controls permissions. Opened manage-queues-app, Copilot release notes and copilot-teams-calling-transcription; none is a dedicated mobile Copilot feature page.

claims.claim: Eligible Copilot-licensed users can query recorded calls they can access in shared call history.
claims.quote: Open Copilot from a recorded call in shared call history. This feature does not change how call recordings are created, stored, or accessed.

claims.claim: A recording template's representative recording-access selection cannot be modified after template creation.
claims.quote: Select which call recordings call queue representatives (agents) can access. Authorized users have access by default. This setting can't be modified once the template is created.

claims.claim: The automatic recording template defines the SharePoint storage location of recordings and transcripts.
claims.quote: An automatic recording template for Call Queue defines where, in SharePoint, recordings and transcripts will be stored

claims.claim: Copilot interactions are automatically audited when organizational auditing is enabled.
claims.quote: The system automatically logs these activities as part of Audit (Standard). If your organization enables auditing, you don't need to take extra steps to configure auditing support for Copilot and AI applications.

claims.claim: Copilot audit logs are accessible and searchable under Audit in the Microsoft Purview portal.
claims.quote: Access Copilot audit logs by using the Microsoft Purview portal and selecting Audit.

claims.claim: Microsoft 365 Copilot user prompts and responses can be covered by retention policies.
claims.quote: Retention policies for AI apps include user prompts and responses for Microsoft 365 Copilot and Copilot Studio

claims.claim: Retention copies of Copilot messages are stored in a hidden user-mailbox folder.
claims.quote: Data from generative AI messages is stored in a hidden folder in the mailbox of the user who runs the AI app.

claims.claim: Compliance administrators can search those hidden-mailbox message copies with eDiscovery tools.
claims.quote: This hidden folder isn't designed to be directly accessible to users or administrators, but instead, store data that compliance administrators can search with eDiscovery tools.

claims.claim: The general Copilot interaction auditing rules cover this Microsoft Copilot experience.
claims.quote: The system automatically generates audit logs when a user interacts with Copilot, Cowork, or an AI application.

claims.claim: Microsoft 365 Copilot retention coverage includes prompts and responses in this experience.
claims.quote: Retention policies for AI apps include user prompts and responses for Microsoft 365 Copilot and Copilot Studio

claims.claim: Learn does not document a separate permission for Copilot in the Queues app.
claims.quote: Searched: Queues app Copilot Mobile policy permission disable; Copilot Queues policy permissions disable Set-CsTeamsCallingPolicy. Read manage-queues-app and copilot-teams-calling-transcription; found licensing and general calling controls, no separate Queues Copilot permission.

claims.claim: The roadmap and notice describe question answering for human follow-up, not autonomous action.
claims.quote: Understand a customer conversation and decide on a follow-up without reviewing the full call.

claims.where: controls[4]; Risk assessment; Governance guidance; Governance controls
claims.claim: No separate mobile Queues Copilot tenant switch is documented on either UI or automation surfaces.
claims.quote: Searched: Queues app Copilot Mobile policy permission disable; Copilot Queues policy permissions disable Set-CsTeamsCallingPolicy. Read manage-queues-app, copilot-teams-calling-transcription and calling policy reference excerpts; no separate mobile Queues switch found.

claims.claim: The documented app availability route is Teams admin center > Teams apps > Manage apps > Actions > Org-wide app settings > Microsoft apps.
claims.quote: Navigate to Teams apps > Manage apps. Select Actions > Org-wide app settings > Microsoft apps. Select Off and Save.

claims.claim: Turning off the Queues app by that org-wide setting also turns off Insights and Tasks rather than just Copilot.
claims.quote: You can turn off the Queues app via the Teams admin center. However, doing so also turns off other Microsoft apps like Insights and Tasks.

claims.claim: No automation equivalent is documented for the Microsoft apps org-wide setting used by this row.
claims.quote: Searched: Teams org-wide app settings Microsoft apps PowerShell Graph disable Queues app; Set-CsTeamsClientConfiguration AllowAppsInTeams; org wide Microsoft apps settings API powershell. Read app management and cmdlet excerpts; app permission policy cmdlet says do not use it.

claims.claim: Licences can be assigned under Microsoft 365 admin center > Billing > Licenses > product > Assign licenses.
claims.quote: In the admin center, go to the Billing > Licenses page. Select a product. On the product details page, select Assign licenses.

claims.claim: POST /v1.0/users/{id | userPrincipalName}/assignLicense assigns or removes user licences.
claims.quote: Add or remove licenses for the user to enable or disable their use of Microsoft cloud offerings that the company has licenses to. POST /users/{id | userPrincipalName}/assignLicense
claims.fix: Keep the call unchanged. Add to controls[0].note: 'The request body uses addLicenses to assign licences and removeLicenses to remove them.' The v1.0 reference documents both properties.

claims.claim: Supported delegated licence-assignment roles include License Administrator and User Administrator.
claims.quote: The following least privileged roles are supported for this operation: Directory Writers; License Administrator; User Administrator

claims.claim: A custom role with microsoft.directory/users/assignLicense can alternatively authorize the signed-in user.
claims.quote: the signed-in user must be assigned a supported Microsoft Entra role or a custom role with the microsoft.directory/users/assignLicense role permission.

claims.claim: LicenseAssignment.ReadWrite.All is an application permission for assignLicense.
claims.quote: Application | LicenseAssignment.ReadWrite.All

claims.claim: A recording template is assigned at Teams admin center > Voice > Call queue > call queue > Templates > Automatic recording template.
claims.quote: go to Voice > Call queue. Select the call queue you want to have automatic recording for. On the Templates tab, scroll to find the Automatic recording template section.

claims.claim: Set-CsCallQueue -Identity <Guid> -AutoRecordingTemplateId <String> applies an automatic recording template, subject to the stated private-preview restriction.
claims.quote: Set-CsCallQueue -Identity <Guid>; [-AutoRecordingTemplateId <String>]. The AutoRecordingTemplateId parameter indicates the Auto Recording template to apply to the call queue.

claims.claim: Assigning a template or managing its queue authorized users requires the Teams administrator also to be a SharePoint site administrator for that site.
claims.quote: To assign an automatic recording template to a call queue or manage its authorized users list, the Teams administrator must also be a SharePoint site administrator for the site used by the template.

claims.claim: The calling policy Copilot setting is at Teams admin center > Voice > Calling policies > policy > Copilot.
claims.quote: Under Voice, select Calling policies. Either select an existing policy or create a new one. From the dropdown for the Copilot setting, select On, On with saved transcript required, or Off.

claims.claim: Set-CsTeamsCallingPolicy -Identity <policy name> -Copilot Disabled turns off Copilot under a calling policy.
claims.quote: To turn off Copilot for calls, use the following command: Set-CsTeamsCallingPolicy -Identity <policy name> -Copilot Disabled

claims.claim: Teams calling policies are documented as controlling Copilot in one-to-one and group calls.
claims.quote: Teams calling policies control Copilot in one-to-one and group calls.

claims.claim: The cited calling-policy documentation does not confirm its reach to the shared-history Queues Copilot experience.
claims.quote: Searched: Copilot Queues policy permissions disable Set-CsTeamsCallingPolicy. Read copilot-teams-calling-transcription: applies to 1:1 Teams and PSTN calls; describes call participants and their transcripts, not Queues shared-history access. No explicit Queues applicability found.

claims.claim: Shared Call History enabled on the queue is a documented automatic-recording prerequisite.
claims.quote: Shared Call History in enabled on the call queue.

claims.claim: The automatic-recording setup page says explicit recording consent must be Off.
claims.quote: Explicit recording consent must be Off.

claims.claim: Microsoft recommends confirming automatic recording is on for queues where users should use Copilot.
claims.quote: Confirm that automatic recording is turned on for the call queues where you want users to use Copilot.

claims.claim: Microsoft recommends reviewing Microsoft 365 Copilot and Teams Premium licence assignments.
claims.quote: Review Microsoft 365 Copilot and Teams Premium license assignments for the users who will use the feature.

claims.claim: Recording templates are created under Teams admin center > Voice > Templates and resources > Templates > Automatic Recording > Add.
claims.quote: go to Voice > Templates and resources. Select Templates. Select Automatic Recording as the template type. Select Add to create a new Automatic Recording template.

claims.claim: The Set-CsCallQueue reference restricts AutoRecordingTemplateId to Voice applications private-preview customers.
claims.quote:
-AutoRecordingTemplateId
Voice applications private preview customers only.

claims.claim: The cmdlet reference warns that saving the queue through Teams admin center removes that setting.
claims.quote: Saving a call queue configuration through Teams admin center will remove this setting.

claims.claim: The setup page's August 13, 2026 update says automatic recording can be configured through PowerShell, differing from the cmdlet restriction.
claims.quote:
August 13, 2026
Automatic Recording for Call Queue can be configured via PowerShell.

claims.where: Governance guidance: Before rollout, automatic recording bullet
claims.claim: Teams admin center > Voice > Call queue is the starting page for checking automatic recording.
claims.quote: go to Voice > Call queue. Select the call queue you want to have automatic recording for. On the Templates tab, scroll to find the Automatic recording template section.
claims.fix: Expand the shortened parenthetical path to 'Teams admin center > Voice > Call queue > call queue > Templates > Automatic recording template', matching controls[1].ui.
